messages:
Anna: Quick sync — we keep running into footguns when pagination meets retries across SDKs. TS autopager retries a page and duplicates items, Go's cursor is awkward to resume, Python users want both sync+async ergonomics. Proposal: one transport-agnostic Cursor interface + server-issued resume tokens + an optional short-lived checkpoint lease.
Jamal: +1. Can you sketch the shape? specifically how retries avoid dupes when a page partially succeeds?
Anna: Sketch: server always returns an opaque resume_token for each page (monotonic). SDKs use that token after a failed attempt to request the next page. For in-flight partial success, server supports a per-page "checkpoint_id" that lets the client ask for remaining items since checkpoint. If absent, client falls back to resume_token semantics.
Sylvie: For Go, we need to preserve context.Context for cancellation and avoid goroutine leaks. API shape I'd prefer: iterator := client.List(ctx, params)
iterator.Next(ctx) -> (item, err)
iterator.Resume(ctx, token) // optional
That fits with existing patterns.
Mike: For TS/Python, async iterators are the norm. We can expose the same resume_token on the iterator object so users can persist it. Eg in TS: const it = client.listItems(params); for await (const i of it) {} console.log(it.resumeToken)
Lee: How do retries look under the hood? If a transport-level retry automatically retries the same HTTP request, the server needs idempotency so we don't get duplicates. I suggest we add an optional header X-Resume-Nonce: <opaque> that conveys client-side attempt id. Server dedups per resume_token + nonce window.
Anna: Exactly — flow: 1) client requests page -> server returns items + resume_token (and maybe checkpoint_id). 2) client starts processing. 3) if client/network error while requesting next page, it reuses resume_token and sends X-Resume-Nonce. Server returns the next slice deterministically.
Jamal: Edge cases: long-running processing + resume token TTL. If token expires, what do we do? Backstop: server can return 410 with explanation; SDK surfaces a typed ExpiredResumeTokenError and optionally attempts a server-side rewind endpoint (if supported) to re-run from a safe anchor (e.g., cursor to last acknowledged id).
Sylvie: For Go we should make Resume/token methods thread-safe. Also recommend we expose a light-weight Snapshot() -> token so platform tasks can persist progress.
Mike: UX question: do we encourage users to call it.snapshot() periodically or should SDK auto-checkpoint every N items? My vote: SDK autosave every N items (configurable) and expose checkpoint hooks for app-level ack.
Anna: Autosave default: every 500 items or 30s, whichever earlier. Make config overridable per-call: list_items(checkpoint_every=1000). For large paged workloads this reduces manual work.
Lee: Transport choices: for streaming endpoints (server-streaming) we can't always get page tokens. Suggest we treat streaming as an append-only stream that exposes a lightweight sequence offset; server returns last_offset periodically and supports resume by offset. That keeps semantics consistent.
Jamal: Implementation note: Don't conflate resume_token (opaque) with logical offsets. Best to keep resume_token opaque but server docs must state monotonicity/TTL. SDK shouldn't parse tokens.
Anna: Agreed. Also decision: SDK surfaces both resumeToken and an error model. Errors: RetryableError (client should retry transparently), ExpiredResumeTokenError, NonRetryableError. Make these language-native exception/types.
Sylvie: For Go: define interfaces in the client package, not runtime internals. Example:

```
type Cursor[T any] interface {
  Next(ctx context.Context) (T, error)
  Resume(ctx context.Context, token string) error
  Token() string
}
```

Keep it simple.
Mike: For Python, propose parity: cursor = client.list_items(...)
- sync: for item in cursor:
- async: async for item in cursor.async_iter():
cursor.token -> str
cursor.save_checkpoint()
Anna: Quick code snippets to show how SDK will use X-Resume-Nonce header (pseudo):

```
// client retry loop
nonce := newNonce()
req.Header.Set("X-Resume-Nonce", nonce)
resp := transport.Do(req)
if resp.Status == 200 { // server dedupes using resume_token + nonce
  use(resp)
}
```

```
# python async usage
async for item in client.list_items(...):
    process(item)
    # library auto-checkpoints in background
```

Lee: Tests we need: 1) simulate partial page success + broken connection 2) token expiry 3) cross-language token roundtrip (TS -> server -> Go) 4) streaming resume by offset.
Jamal: Also we should add a benchmark for memory/latency impact of autosave default frequency.
Anna: Action items: Anna -> write mini-RFC w/ sketches + example HTTP contract (resume_token, checkpoint_id, X-Resume-Nonce). Sylvie -> add Go Cursor interface PR. Mike -> add TS/py iterator shape examples for docs. Lee -> draft server dedupe TTL and 410 semantics. Aim for decision next week. :thumbsup:
